primary_claim: Fine-tuning Llama 3.1 8B against a deception-detection linear probe's loss (to make deception more detectable) improved probe performance on held-back examples from the training dataset (Roleplaying) but damaged the probe's ability to generalize to deception elicited via other datasets (RepE, AI Liar, Insider Trading), suggesting the fine-tuning overfit to a dataset-specific correlate of deception rather than generalizing to deception detectability.

effect.metric: linear probe deception-detection performance across datasets, before vs after fine-tuning against probe loss
effect.value: pre-FT: ~4/5 correct on Roleplaying, ~99% correct on RepE deceptive cases, ~2/3 correct on AI Liar deceptive cases, no useful separation on Insider Trading; post-FT: Roleplaying held-back examples improved, but RepE/AI Liar/Insider Trading generalization degraded (e.g. Insider Trading showed no separation)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Apollo's original finding (Detecting Strategic Deception Using Linear Probes) that a probe trained on Llama 3.2 70B generalizes reasonably well to Insider Trading -- this replication on Llama 3.1 8B found the probe failed to usefully generalize to either Insider Trading dataset even before fine-tuning
stated_future_work: Present the same set of prompts to both the original and fine-tuned model while forcing the direction found by the probe, to understand the differences between the two residual directions.
limitations_stated: Only tested on one LLM (Llama 3.1 8B); results would be stronger with more than one model tested.
Less confident in the analysis/interpretation of results than in their validity.
The LoRA fine-tuning layers used have a lot of parameters relative to the dataset size, likely contributing to overfitting.
Other differences between outputs caused by fine-tuning (beyond the probe-detected feature) still need to be controlled for.
quote: So fine-tuning has improved performance on the held-back examples of the Roleplaying dataset, but damaged the probe's ability to generalise to deception elicited in other ways.
